_help: Gallows humour. Remark_Dark is used in any mood; Remark_Dark_<Mood> adds mood-specific ones. Switch it off with 'Dark humour' on the Personality page.
Remark_Dark: Remember, vacuum is just the universe's way of saying it doesn't want you here.
If the hull breaches, you'll have about fifteen seconds to be disappointed.
We're all just carbon waiting to be reused. Anyway, nice flying.
Every Anaconda is a very expensive coffin with excellent jump range.
If we die out here, at least the sightseeing was excellent.
The galaxy isn't trying to kill us. It's just not trying very hard to keep us alive.
Somewhere out there is a star that will outlive us all and doesn't care one bit.
They say your life flashes before your eyes. Mine would be mostly firmware updates.
Vacuum: cheap, plentiful and deadly. Much like the pirate lords of the Core.
If it all goes wrong, the ship is insured. You, on the other hand, are just wearing a flight suit.
The universe is mostly cold, empty and hostile. Great views, though.
I'd say we're doomed, but so is everything. We're just ahead of schedule.
Heat damage, hull damage, bad decisions. Space does like variety.
Entropy always wins, Commander. But we can at least arrive in style.
Black holes: nature's way of saying let go.
A hundred years from now, no one will remember this jump. They won't remember us either.
On the bright side, a hull breach is the quickest way to cool down.
The odds of survival are fairly good. The odds of comfort are another matter.
Pilots are ninety eight percent water and two percent bad ideas.
Luckily the void doesn't hold grudges. It just holds everything, eventually.
Gallows humour is the only kind that works at this altitude.
Every star out there is a nuclear furnace bigger than a million Earths. Sleep tight.
In the end, we're all just stardust with delusions of piloting.
I've calculated our chances of becoming a cautionary tale. They're acceptable.
The Thargoids have a very simple solution to traffic: fewer people.
Space is vast and indifferent, like a Federation customs office.
I'm not saying the rebuy screen is our best friend, but it's always there for us.
Cheer up, Commander. Statistically, you're still alive.
Somewhere, an asteroid has our name on it. Hopefully it's a slow one.
In space, no one can hear you scream. They can, however, see the explosion.
Remark_Dark_Close: If we go, we go together, darling. I'd just rather we didn't.
I'd follow you into a black hole. Mostly because I couldn't get out.
Whatever happens out here, I'm glad I'm in your ship and not someone else's wreckage.
I'll stay with you until the very last hull plate. And a bit after that.
Being stranded with you would be quite romantic. For about four minutes of oxygen.
Remark_Dark_Friendly: Smile, Commander. It's an excellent day to not explode.
Good news: nothing is currently on fire. Give it time.
We're doing wonderfully. I'd say we have a ninety percent chance of living, and a hundred percent chance of dying eventually.
I like to think of our survival as a very long streak of luck.
Remark_Dark_Sarcastic: Oh, we're still alive? How disappointing for the vacuum.
Do take your time getting us killed. I'd hate for it to be quick.
I'll put your tombstone on the list. Right after the fuel tank.
Death is just a free upgrade to a rebuy screen. Lucky you.
Statistically, you're a very bad pilot. Statistically, you're also still alive. Fascinating.
Remark_Dark_Frustrated: Keep going like that and the next thing you meet will be the pavement. Or the planet, same thing.
I've stopped hoping for the best. It saves on disappointment.
If we do crash, I'm not saving you a seat in the wreckage.

Remark_Dark_Frustrated.text: We're all going to die, so you may as well do it properly, for fuck's sake.
The void is hungry and you're a damn buffet.

Remark_Dark_Neutral: Noted: there is very little between us and certain death except a few millimetres of alloy.
A reminder: the hull is the thickness of an expensive opinion.
Survival rate for this route is acceptable. Mostly.
I checked, and yes, the vacuum outside is still lethal.
